title: Metals let electric charge move through them easily
summary: Metals such as copper, silver, and aluminum are electrical conductors, because charge moves through them easily.
body: OpenStax Physics says materials can be sorted by whether they let charge move. If charge moves easily, as in metals, the material is a conductor. In metals the outer electrons are loosely bound, so not much energy is needed to make them move. Copper, silver, and aluminum are named as good conductors. An excess charge placed on a conducting object spreads over the outer surface, because the like charges push apart and they are free to move. Insulators, where charge stays put, are a different card. This one does not say what voltage is safe to touch.
